subject: Enable application to diplay output before processing completes

messages.author: ea6b1cd9e71466ee
messages.subject: Enable application to diplay output before processing completes
parts:
I've recently run into this issue twice and I'm wondering if there's a way around it:

For web UIs that are used to kick off long-running processes, it is often desirable to have the UI display a message like "Your request has been submitted" so that the user knows they did in fact click the correct "submit" button and that the application is not waiting on them for any other input.

In attempting to implement this, we realized that apparently Shiny orders operations in a way that groups all processing before any displaying. For example, we tried something like this:

output$displayMessage <- renderText({
  if (qcFlag == 1) {
    reactive$launchProcessFlag <- 1
    print("Your request has been submitted")
  }
  else {print("QC Error")}
})

output$launchProcess <- renderText({
  if (reactive$launchProcessFlag == 1) {
    launchProcess()
  }
})


However, we noticed that the error message was not displaying until after the script actually completed. The way we're currently providing confirmation is sending the user an email as part of the long process mentioned above, but it's not ideal for the user to have no visual confirmation and to have to check their email.

So, is it correct that Shiny saves all of its 'displaying' until after all processing? If so, is there a way to get around it without going the route of setting up a REST api that waits to run the script? 


Thanks!
